card.name: "with" after a physiological effect
card.fires_on: The word "with" right after a named clinical effect or process, where it introduces a resulting consequence such as marked hypotension or circulatory collapse. Seen in overdose and adverse-effect passages.

modes.label: Effect with consequence
modes.description: "with" follows a condition noun like vasodilation or dissemination and introduces a resulting finding.
modes.example: excessive peripheral vasodilation<< with>> marked hypotension

modes.label: Process with complication
modes.description: "with" links a process such as diuresis, dehydration or stone formation to a serious downstream complication.
modes.example: blood volume reduction<< with>> circulatory collapse and possibly vascular thromb

card.writes: It seems to push the model toward words about harm and adverse outcomes after "with", though the promoted tokens are mixed.
card.plain: It marks the word "with" when a drug effect is about to be followed by the bad result that comes with it.
